decisions.quote: The present report is the second large-scale validation study of the PDSQ in psychiatric out-patients. Because some of the sizes of the diagnostic groups in the initial report were modest, it is important to determine whether the recommended cut-off scores to screen for psychiatric disorders remained the same in a replication study.
decisions.reason: The supplied primary source contains only the title, author line (M. Zimmerman; I. Chelminski), and abstract, with no full text or reference list. The abstract explicitly describes an empirical replication study testing whether the diagnostic performance (receiver operating characteristic curve analysis) and recommended subscale cut-off scores of the Psychiatric Diagnostic Screening Questionnaire (PDSQ) from 'the initial validation study' / 'the initial report' hold in a new sample of 670 psychiatric out-patients, but gives no in-text citation or bibliographic details for that initial report. Consequently, the blind coder recorded an unnamed target placeholder (target_index 0). Shipped row 658 (Zimmerman & Mattia, 2001, 'A Self-Report Scale to Help Make Psychiatric Diagnoses', Archives of General Psychiatry 58(8): 787, DOI 10.1001/archpsyc.58.8.787) is by the PDSQ's developer Mark Zimmerman and likely represents the initial PDSQ validation report, but without the full text or reference list the supplied primary evidence does not settle whether shipped row 658 is the exact initial validation report re-tested here rather than a related PDSQ scale-development paper. No prior adjudication or prior state file existed for this work.
